# My generated byte conversion checkpoint

I continue task_c6b2a040c1434fc784a9d46c02a4981e after raw VM PR929. I implement
matching native C and LLVM/Wasm conversion before source and reconstruction.
Computed INT converts modulo256; U8 retains identity; every other tag fails.
No heap allocation, floating conversion, enum coercion or new entry ABI occurs.

My native classifier publishes an exact TAG_U8 scalar fact in tagged storage.
Emission uses defined uint8_t conversion and a checked tagged helper. A known
non-integer representation emits the existing native invariant failure; an
unresolved representation refuses translation. Every consumed source is evaluated
once. Tagged storage support is selected even when a program has no PUSH_U8.

LLVM extracts the tag, checks INT or U8, truncates payload to i8 and zero-extends
back to the i64 carrier with result TAG_U8. In managed mode the existing check
records first failure; the consumed operand remains in the existing temporary
root ledger until release, followed by normal error cleanup. Wrong STRING or
aggregate input never becomes a successful byte or a raw pointer dereference.
Wasm uses this actual LLVM route, not a separate interpreter.

I explicitly add CAST_U8 to the shared closed scalar transfer and managed shape
result table only alongside matching emitters. The latter also supplies the
private non-admitting mixed query's opcode inventory: its future generated plan
must account for the new no-allocation scalar operation. Service-first, owned,
passive and all other separate authority selectors keep their existing checks;
reconstruction and source producers remain unimplemented and refused here.
